subject: Avalon Health — Discovery alignment: SDK function-call & streaming approach
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rodriguez <maya@avalonhealth.com>, Dev Team <dev@avalonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Avalon Health — Discovery alignment: SDK function-call & streaming approach

Hi Maya / team,

Thanks again for a productive call today — appreciate the candid product context and the latency/cost constraints you're operating under. Quick recap so we're aligned and so we can move to a focused technical proposal: 

1) Primary pain & goals (as we heard)
- Clinical triage assistant must return structured recommendations (diagnosis code, urgency, recommended next step) for each patient note with deterministic fields for downstream rules.
- Real-time experience: <200ms server-side median for single-turn responses at 8 req/s initially, expected growth to 40 req/s in 6 months.
- Ranking: you want a candidate list of suggestions with relevance scores to feed into the rules engine — embeddings + rerank looks preferable to you.

2) Product / integration fit we discussed
- SDK changes: lightweight streaming client (token-streaming to UI), explicit function-call wiring for structured output (we'll provide schema examples), and an embeddings endpoint combined with a reranking step.
- Streaming: we recommend continuous streaming for the LLM response, but a final structured function call payload for downstream deterministic parsing. This lets UI show progressive tokens while ensuring the final JSON is validated.
- Fallbacks & cost: route to a smaller quantized model for non-critical signals; keep the high-capacity variant for structured outputs and rerank when confidence is low.

3) Technical asks from Avalon (please confirm):
- A: Can you confirm expected p95 latency SLOs from the client side and peak concurrency per user session? (you mentioned spikes up to 12 concurrent sessions).
- B: Do you require end-to-end encryption with customer-managed KMS for logs/artifacts?
- C: Example CSV of 200 sample patient notes we can use for a short eval (anonymized).

4) Proposed next steps & owners
- Redwood: draft a one-page integration pattern showing the streaming + function-call flow, plus an embeddings + rerank example (target: 2 business days). [Attachment: av-demo-notes.pdf]
- Avalon: confirm items A–C above and share an internal contact for security/compliance (if different from Maya) — target: EOD Wed.
- Joint: schedule a 60-min technical working session to walk the SDK changes and proto schema (we suggested Thurs morning).

Attachments: av-demo-notes.pdf (call notes & suggested function-call schema), proposal-endpoints-v1.xlsx (placeholder with endpoints we intend to propose).

If the above matches your notes, I'll turn this into a short integration proposal and include an ops checklist for Dedicated vs Hosted options.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: av-demo-notes.pdf]

Subject: Re: Avalon Health — Discovery alignment: SDK function-call & streaming approach

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with our internal takeaways. Quick answers inline: 

> A: Confirm expected p95 latency SLOs ...
We are targeting 250ms p95 for the median clinician flow; 150ms interactive UI target would be ideal but we know that's tough for server-side. Peak concurrency initial is ~10 concurrent inference calls per clinician during peak ( ~40 overall system-wide).

> B: KMS for logs/artifacts
Yes — we need customer-managed KMS for any persisted logs and want to understand how Redwood handles ephemeral request traces. I'll introduce our security lead (CC'd: security@avalonhealth.com) in the next email.

> C: 200 sample patient notes
We can deliver an anonymized sample set next week. I'll have Dev attach to the Drive folder and share a link.

Also: for reranking, can you outline whether you expect a single embeddings call per request versus batch scoring? We're leaning toward batch scoring against a per-session candidate pool.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Rodriguez
Product Lead, Avalon Health

Maya — thanks for the quick confirmations and for looping in the security contact. Final alignment below and immediate next steps: 

Confirmed items:
- Targets: 250ms p95 (system) / peak concurrency starting ~40 req/s.
- Security: customer-managed KMS required for persisted logs; Redwood will provide an architectural note on ephemeral traces and will not persist raw patient text unless explicitly toggled.
- Rerank approach: Redwood recommends batching embeddings per clinician-session and performing an in-memory candidate rerank to keep latency predictable. We will include both single-call and batch scoring examples in the docs.

Deliverables (owners & ETA):
- Laura: Integration pattern doc (streaming + function-call wiring) + ops checklist (target: Fri 21 Aug). [Deliverable includes example function-call JSON schema and progressive-token streaming diagram; attached: proposal-endpoints-v1.xlsx]
- Ava: Prototype function-call schema (diagnosis, urgency, rule_flags) + example SDK snippet for streaming (target: Thu EOD).
- Ben: Cost/commit estimate including a Dedicated reserve comparison (target: Fri).
- Avalon: Anonymized sample notes in shared Drive (target: next Tue), and confirmation of security contact acceptance of the KMS pattern.

If there are no objections, I'll book the technical working session for Thursday 08:30 PT. Please reply with availability.

Appreciate the momentum — will send the integration doc as soon as it's ready.
